newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: Zambia plans export processing zones.
newsitem.headline: Zambia plans export processing zones.

text.p: The Zambian government said on Friday it would soon set up export processing zones to encourage trade to the outside world.

"The government has taken a firm decision to establish export processing zones within which manufacturers will be accorded a number of fiscal benefits," a Zambian Ministry of Commerce and Trade official told Reuters.
"The Zambia Investment Centre is already working on proposals on the establishment of these zones," he added.
He said the tourist resort of Livingstone bordering Zimbabwe was a likely area to be turned into an export processing zone.
"We are set on moving away from being an economy that produces primary commodities on behalf of other countries where real and substantial value is added," he said.
Among other things, the government would encourage the establishment of companies to cut and polish gemstones, manufacture copper-cased products and processed timber.
"Minerals such as copper, which as you know is in abundance, offer business opportunity in the making of various copper-based products such as copper tubes, copper rods, copper sheets and cables.
"Our government's policy is to discourage the exportation of unprocessed timber and encourage the production of timber-based products," the official said.
Zambia's export earnings dropped by 18 percent to $974.9 million in 1996 from $1,185.9 million the previous year, largely because of falling copper prices.
